core.title: Admit composite dispatch keys only with a behavioral difference and a single field:value discriminant
core.given: A dispatch map routes artifacts to user/system flows, and a composite (artifact_urn, discriminant) -> user_system_flow_id dispatch key exists or is proposed.
core.when: That composite dispatch key is introduced, changed or assessed (in a plan, acceptance, doc or review).
core.then: Treat the composite key as exceptional: permit it only with a behavioral_difference justification and a discriminant that is exactly one field:value.
prefer: Key dispatch by artifact_urn alone; use a composite key only when there is a behavioral difference to justify it.
State the behavioral_difference as the observable behavior that differs between the routed user/system flows.
Write the discriminant as exactly one field:value.
avoid: Composite keys with a missing or empty behavioral_difference justification.
Discriminants that are not exactly one field:value (e.g. several fields combined, or no field:value at all).
Composite keys used for organisational convenience where user/system flow behavior is the same.
core.why: The dispatch map is a registry mapping an artifact to a user/system flow by default; unjustified composite keys break that default and hide why one artifact routes to different user/system flows.
evidence: Each composite entry in the dispatch map has a non-empty behavioral_difference and a discriminant that is exactly one field:value.
verification: A composite key is a dispatch key of shape (artifact_urn, discriminant) -> user_system_flow_id; dispatch entries keyed by artifact_urn alone are outside the check's scope.
The check flags a composite dispatch entry whose behavioral_difference justification is missing or empty.
The check flags a composite dispatch entry whose discriminant is not exactly one field:value.
The check scans the artifact that holds the dispatch entries; its concrete kind comes from the profile's plan artifact kinds.
Disposition strict: every finding fails; severity 3.
A validator of this convention enforces it over the dispatch map; the concrete validator/test id is realization-specific.

values: dispatch map / dispatch registry holding (artifact_urn[, discriminant]) -> user_system_flow_id dispatch entries
composite (artifact_urn, discriminant) -> user_system_flow_id dispatch key introduced
composite dispatch key changed (discriminant or justification)
composite dispatch key under assessment or reported by the convention check

fires: A composite (artifact_urn, discriminant) -> user_system_flow_id dispatch key is added to the dispatch map, by any actor in any phase.
An existing composite dispatch key's discriminant or behavioral_difference justification is changed.
A plan, review or audit assesses existing composite dispatch keys for admissibility.
A composite key is proposed whose discriminant combines two field:value pairs.
doesNotFire: A dispatch entry keyed by artifact_urn alone is added or changed.
User/system flow or product capability documents are edited without introducing, changing or assessing any dispatch key.
A user/system flow handler is implemented without touching or assessing dispatch keys.

neutralityNotes: The rule is almost entirely stack-neutral: it governs the planning model (dispatch map, user/system flows, artifact_urn, discriminant, behavioral_difference, field:value), which is ATDD meta-model vocabulary rather than stack mechanics, so those terms are kept in the core. The only stack datum is the concrete artifact kind that holds dispatch entries, routed through roles.plan_artifact.kinds. The validator/test reference (evidence[0]) and the rule term id 'composite_key' (verifier_detail[0]) are realization details left out of the core; severity 3 and strict disposition are per-rule data carried in core:verification, not profile keys. Facts activation.facts[2] and [3] still need new observers in any stack, as recorded in their observability.
